text:
ashley: incident-bot alerted: canary rollout 2026-03-15T09:12Z failing health checks, crashlooping encoder pods. high 5xx rate on /v1/generate from canary subset. paging oncall now. :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident triggered (INC-2026-0315-17). Acknowledgement required by oncall.

marta: acked. seeing HPA spike to 18 replicas for canary-nn; most are CrashLoopBackOff. can we pause the rollout and flip the feature flag to route traffic away from canary?

lee: holding rollout via deploy-bot: `deploy pause canary/encoder-rollout --id 2026-0315-09`

devops-bot: rollout paused.

sam: reflagging: add immediate kill-switch on traffic-router -> stitcher. can we set flag encoder_canary=false? That should drain traffic out of canary quickly.

ashley: flipping flag now (experiment-service): `curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/flags -d '{"encoder_canary":false}'` -> returned 200. monitor routing.

monitoring-bot: Canary traffic dropped from 12% -> 0.5% over 70s. 5xx rate on production overall down from 3.2% -> 0.9% and trending.

marta: good. digging into why pods crashloop. grabbing container logs from one canary pod:

```
2026-03-15T09:10:42Z ERROR encoder main - assertion failed: kv_cache_size negative
2026-03-15T09:10:42Z FATAL unhandled exception - invalid kv offset 0xffffffff
stack: at runtime/kv.cc:214
-- repeated on startup --
```

lee: that looks like a model shard/manifest mismatch after the new release. manifest version is 7c4f8 but nodes pulled 7c3e1. possible partial rollout where image + manifest drifted.

sam: checking registry and release jobs. release pipeline shows build 2026-0315-09 pushed to gcr at 09:05, but manifest update job failed on two nodes during rollout window (timeout).

ashley: so we have inconsistent model artifact and runtime expectation -> crashloop. canary traffic kill-switch prevented customer impact from spreading. next step: rollback canary pods to previous image and ensure manifest consistency.

marta: oncall playbook step: scale down HPA to 0 for canary to stop thrashing while we roll back? pros/cons?

lee: if we scale to 0 we'll kill pods (fine) but HPA might re-create them if metrics step in. we should set `kubectl scale --replicas=0 deploy/encoder-canary` and annotate to disable HPA temporarily.

sam: executing rollback command: `kubectl set image deploy/encoder-canary encoder=registry.redwood/encoder:2026-0314-2200 --namespace=prod`

devops-bot: command accepted. starting rollout-back: `rollout restart deploy/encoder-canary`

ashley: while rollback runs, we should inform CS about potential user-facing failures for the last 8 minutes. notifying cs-team. @cs-team please prepare a status note: small set of API users experienced elevated 5xx rates 09:05-09:13 UTC, we mitigated.

marta: adding a short mitigation note to the incident ticket: rollback initiated, traffic routed away, investigating root cause (artifact drift).

monitoring-bot: New pods coming up. readiness probes passing for 3/3 on updated image. 5xx rate for affected endpoints back to baseline 0.3% in 2m.

lee: verifying manifests on nodes: `sha256sum /opt/models/manifest.json` shows 7c4f8 now on the updated pods. older nodes still had 7c3e1 but they were removed from rotation.

sam: closing the immediate customer-impact loop: rolling back the canary and flip-off flag prevented wider outage. we should still schedule a canary audit job and fix the manifest publishing race.

ashley: action items:
- sam: create hotfix to make manifest update transactional and retry across nodes (owner: sam)
- lee: add guard in rollout to verify manifest checksum before marking pod ready (owner: lee)
- marta: run through postmortem template and include impact window + mitigation steps (owner: marta)
- infra: add alert for manifest-version-mismatch when runtime check fails (owner: infra team)

marta: for the pager duty timeline: triggered 09:12, acked 09:12:30, flag flipped 09:14, rollback started 09:17, baseline restored 09:20. logging these to incident ticket.

ashley: any customer escalations? cs-team says 4 enterprise customers reported transient 5xx and got auto-retries. no SLA breach so far, but we should call any customers who saw degraded latency >30s.

lee: I'll handle outreach for the three customers matched to canary routing. tagging account owners.

sam: small note: we saw HPA surge due to unhealthy readiness probes and metrics scraping from crashloops. consider softer scaling thresholds for canaries.

devops-bot: Rollback completed successfully at 09:18:22 UTC. `kubectl rollout status deployment/encoder-canary: success`

monitoring-bot: Synthetic checks green at 09:20:10 UTC. No further 5xx spikes in last 15m.

marta: closing oncall handoff in 10m. leaving incident open for postmortem and root-cause fix tracking.

ashley: big thanks to everyone for quick response. tagging for postmortem: sam, lee, marta, ashley. will draft the timeline and link to logs. :thumbsup:
